title: Continuous inhomogeneous cochains and their differential
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $J$ a topological group, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with an $E$-linear $J$-action whose action map $J\times V\to V$ is jointly continuous. The continuous inhomogeneous cochains are $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$ for $n\in\mathbf N$, regarded as abstract $E$-vector spaces. In degree zero evaluation on the unique point identifies $C(J^0,V)$ with $V$. Define the $E$-linear differential by
$$(d^nf)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this means $(d^0v)(g)=gv-v$. The continuous inhomogeneous cochain complex is the nonnegative cochain complex of abstract $E$-vector spaces with these terms and differential. Its cohomology uses the image of the differential without taking its closure. No completeness, local compactness, or discreteness of $V$ is assumed.
